title: Striking the Rider Premium Left Owed When a Rider is Closed
content:
Memorandum of the premium accounting desk on the closing figure struck when a member ends one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders at their own request.

## 1. The figure

The rider premium left owed when a rider is closed at the member's own request is what stands owed on it, less the rider premium refunded for coverage months beyond the day it ends, less the money on the medical plan bill set against it, rounded to the nearest cent and never less than nothing.

## 2. The billing cycle

A billing cycle carries a single coverage month.

## 3. What stands owed

What stands owed is what every charge on the rider premium account comes to less every payment and every credit on it.

## 4. Coverage months beyond the day the rider ends

No coverage month falls beyond the day the rider ends.

## 5. The rate each coverage month is refunded at

The rate each coverage month is refunded at is the amount of the rider premium charge carrying the most money of any standing on the account.

## 6. The ceiling on the refund

The most that may be refunded is the amount of the rider premium charge carrying the most money of any standing on the account, a credit never exceeding the charge it relieves.

## 7. The rider premium refunded

The rider premium refunded is the rate each coverage month is refunded at multiplied by the coverage months beyond the day the rider ends, rounded to the nearest cent, and never more than the most that may be refunded.

## 8. The medical plan bill

The money on the medical plan bill set against what is left owed is nothing. The money left standing on the medical plan bill is what has been paid on it less the medical plan premium charged on it, and is never less than nothing.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

A rider premium account carries charges of 61.50 USD and 61.50 USD, one payment of 61.50 USD and no credit.

1. A billing cycle carries a single coverage month.
2. What stands owed is 123.00 USD less 61.50 USD less nothing, that is 61.50 USD.
3. No coverage month falls beyond the day the rider ends: none.
4. The rate each coverage month is refunded at is the largest charge standing on the account, 61.50 USD.
5. The most that may be refunded is that same 61.50 USD.
6. The rider premium refunded is 61.50 USD multiplied by none, that is nothing, which is not more than the ceiling.
7. The money on the medical plan bill set against what is left owed is nothing.
8. The rider premium left owed is 61.50 USD less nothing less nothing, that is **61.50 USD**.

Every figure above is a hypothetical input.
